block.description:
The Cribl Terraform provider offers a streamlined, repeatable approach for configuring end-to-end infrastructure as code (IaC) and managing resources consistently across Cribl Organizations and Workspaces.

This Preview feature is still being developed. We do not recommend using it in a production environment, because the feature might not be fully tested or optimized for performance, and related documentation could be incomplete.

Complementary API reference documentation is available at https://docs.cribl.io/cribl-as-code/api-reference/. Product documentation is available at https://docs.cribl.io.

ca.description:
Certificate Authority (CA) certificate in PEM format:

Base64-encoded data enclosed by -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE----- delimiters.

If you need to provide a chain, concatenate multiple CA certificates in a single JSON string, each beginning and ending with its own delimiters.

ca_path.description: Path to the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate file.

cert.description:
Certificate in PEM format:

Base64-encoded data enclosed by -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE----- delimiters.

If you need to provide a chain, concatenate multiple certificates in a single JSON string, each beginning and ending with its own delimiters.

cert_expiry_date.description: Certificate expiration date and time as an ISO-8601 UTC string.

cert_path.description: Path to the certificate file.

in_use.description: List of configurations that reference this certificate.

passphrase.description: If the private key is encrypted, the decryption passphrase.

priv_key.description:
Private key for the certificate in PEM format:

Base64-encoded data enclosed by the appropriate delimiters for the key type, such as -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- and -----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----.

Responses do not include the privKey value.

priv_key_path.description: Path to the private key file.

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

region.description: Region where the bucket is located

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

backoff_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to backoff delay after each retry. Valid range: 1-10. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

jitter_percent.description: Random jitter percentage added to backoff delay to prevent thundering herd. Valid range: 0-100. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance

site_id.description: Exabeam site ID. If left blank, @{product} will use the value of the Exabeam site name.

site_name.description: Constant or JavaScript expression to create an Exabeam site name. Values that aren't successfully evaluated will be treated as string constants.

stage_path.description: Filesystem location in which to buffer files, before compressing and moving to final destination. Use performant and stable storage.

streamtags.description: Tags for filtering and grouping in @{product}

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

add_id_to_stage_path.description: Add the Output ID value to staging location

automatic_schema.description: Automatically calculate the schema based on the events of each Parquet file generated

base_file_name.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename prefix (can be constant)

deadletter_enabled.description: If a file fails to move to its final destination after the maximum number of retries, move it to a designated directory to prevent further errors

deadletter_path.description: Storage location for files that fail to reach their final destination after maximum retries are exceeded

dest_path.description: Final destination for the output files

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

extra_http_headers.description: Headers to add to all events

extra_log_types.description: Custom log types. If the value "Custom" is selected in the setting "Default log type" above, the first custom log type in this table will be automatically selected as default log type.

flush_period_sec.description: Maximum time between requests. Small values could cause the payload size to be smaller than the configured Body size limit.

log_text_field.description: Name of the event field that contains the log text to send. If not specified, Stream sends a JSON representation of the whole event.

log_type.description: Default log type value to send to SecOps. Can be overwritten by event field __logType.

max_payload_size_kb.description: Maximum size, in KB, of the request body

pq_max_backpressure_sec.description: How long (in seconds) to wait for backpressure to resolve before engaging the queue

pq_max_buffer_size.description: Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use pqMaxBufferSizeBytes instead.

pq_max_buffer_size_bytes.description: The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 1MB.

pq_max_file_size.description: The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing (KB, MB, etc.)

pq_max_size.description: The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.

pq_path.description: The location for the persistent queue files. To this field's value, the system will append: /<worker-id>/<output-id>.

pq_rate_per_sec.description: Throttling rate (in events per second) to impose while writing to Destinations from PQ. Defaults to 0, which disables throttling.

pq_strict_ordering.description: Use FIFO (first in, first out) processing. Disable to forward new events to receivers before queue is flushed.

region.description: Regional endpoint to send events to

reject_unauthorized.description:
Reject certificates not authorized by a CA in the CA certificate path or by another trusted CA (such as the system's). 
        Enabled by default. When this setting is also present in TLS Settings (Client Side), 
        that value will take precedence.

response_honor_retry_after_header.description: Honor any Retry-After header that specifies a delay (in seconds) no longer than 180 seconds after the retry request. @{product} limits the delay to 180 seconds, even if the Retry-After header specifies a longer delay. When enabled, takes precedence over user-configured retry options. When disabled, all Retry-After headers are ignored.

backoff_rate.description: Base for exponential backoff. A value of 2 (default) means Cribl Stream will retry after 2 seconds, then 4 seconds, then 8 seconds, etc.

http_status.description: The HTTP response status code that will trigger retries

initial_backoff.description: How long, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should wait before initiating backoff. Maximum interval is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).

max_backoff.description: The maximum backoff interval, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should apply. Default (and minimum) is 10,000 ms (10 seconds); maximum is 180,000 ms (180 seconds).

response_retry_settings.description: Automatically retry after unsuccessful response status codes, such as 429 (Too Many Requests) or 503 (Service Unavailable)

safe_headers.description: List of headers that are safe to log in plain text

service_account_credentials.description: Contents of service account credentials (JSON keys) file downloaded from Google Cloud. To upload a file, click the upload button at this field's upper right.

service_account_credentials_secret.description: Select or create a stored text secret

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

backoff_rate.description: Base for exponential backoff. A value of 2 (default) means Cribl Stream will retry after 2 seconds, then 4 seconds, then 8 seconds, etc.

initial_backoff.description: How long, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should wait before initiating backoff. Maximum interval is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).

max_backoff.description: The maximum backoff interval, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should apply. Default (and minimum) is 10,000 ms (10 seconds); maximum is 180,000 ms (180 seconds).

timeout_sec.description: Amount of time, in seconds, to wait for a request to complete before canceling it

total_memory_limit_kb.description: Maximum total size of the batches waiting to be sent. If left blank, defaults to 5 times the max body size (if set). If 0, no limit is enforced.

udm_type.description: Defines the specific format for UDM events sent to Google SecOps. This must match the type of UDM data being sent.

use_round_robin_dns.description: Enable round-robin DNS lookup. When a DNS server returns multiple addresses, @{product} will cycle through them in the order returned.

cache_fill_bytes_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request cache fill bytes as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

cache_hit_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request cache hit as a boolean. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

cache_lookup_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request cache lookup as a boolean. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

cache_validated_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request cache validated with origin server as a boolean. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

concurrency.description: Maximum number of ongoing requests before blocking.

connection_timeout.description: Amount of time (milliseconds) to wait for the connection to establish before retrying

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

file_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry source location file as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentrysourcelocation) for details.

first_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry operation first flag as a boolean. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentryoperation) for details.

flush_period_sec.description: Maximum time between requests. Small values could cause the payload size to be smaller than the configured Max record size.

function_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry source location function as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentrysourcelocation) for details.

id_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry operation ID as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentryoperation) for details.

index_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry log split index as a number. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logsplit) for details.

insert_id_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the insert ID field.

last_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry operation last flag as a boolean. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentryoperation) for details.

latency_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request latency, formatted as <seconds>.<nanoseconds>s (for example, 1.23s). See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

line_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry source location line as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentrysourcelocation) for details.

value_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the label's value.

log_labels.description: Labels to apply to the log entry

log_location_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the folder ID with which log entries should be associated. If Validate and correct log name is enabled, invalid characters (characters other than alphanumerics, forward-slashes, underscores, hyphens, and periods) will be replaced with an underscore.

log_name_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the log name. If Validate and correct log name is enabled, invalid characters (characters other than alphanumerics, forward-slashes, underscores, hyphens, and periods) will be replaced with an underscore.

max_payload_events.description: Max number of events to include in the request body. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_payload_size_kb.description: Maximum size, in KB, of the request body.

payload_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the payload. Must evaluate to a JavaScript object value. If an invalid value is encountered it will result in the default value instead. Defaults to the entire event.

payload_format.description: Format to use when sending payload. Defaults to Text.

producer_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry operation producer as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logentryoperation) for details.

protocol_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request protocol as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

referer_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request referer as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

remote_ip_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request remote IP as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_method_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request method as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_size_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request size as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_url_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request URL as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

resource_type_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the managed resource type field. Must evaluate to one of the valid values [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/api/v2/resource-list#resource-types). Defaults to "global".

value_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the label's value.

resource_type_labels.description: Labels to apply to the managed resource. These must correspond to the valid labels for the specified resource type (see [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/api/v2/resource-list#resource-types)). Otherwise, they will be dropped by Google Cloud Logging.

response_size_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP response size as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

secret.description: Select or create a stored text secret

server_ip_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request server IP as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

service_account_credentials.description: Contents of service account credentials (JSON keys) file downloaded from Google Cloud. To upload a file, click the upload button at this field's upper right.

severity_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the severity field. Must evaluate to one of the severity values supported by Google Cloud Logging [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logseverity) (case insensitive). Defaults to "DEFAULT".

span_id_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the ID of the cloud trace span associated with the current operation in which the log is being written as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

status_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request method as a number. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

trace_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the REST resource name of the trace being written as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

trace_sampled_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the the sampling decision of the span associated with the log entry. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

uid_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry log split UID as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logsplit) for details.

user_agent_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request user agent as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

base_url.description: Base URL of the endpoint used to send events to, such as https://<Your-S1-Tenant>.sentinelone.net. Must begin with http:// or https://, can include a port number, and no trailing slashes. Matches pattern: ^https?://[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?$.

compress.description: Compress the payload body before sending

concurrency.description: Maximum number of ongoing requests before blocking

data_source_category.description: Specify the dataSource.category value to pass as a parameter to SentinelOne AI SIEM. This value helps categorize data and enables additional features. Don't quote this value. The default is security.

data_source_category_expression.description: Define the dataSource.category for events using a JavaScript expression. This value helps categorize data and helps enable extra features in SentinelOne AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes. The default value is 'security'.

data_source_name.description: Specify the dataSource.name value to pass as a parameter to AI SIEM. This value should reflect the type of data being inserted. Don't quote this value. The default is cribl.

data_source_name_expression.description: Define the dataSource.name for events using a JavaScript expression. This value should reflect the type of data being inserted into AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'networkActivity' or 'authLogs').

data_source_vendor.description: Specify the dataSource.vendorvalue to pass as a parameter to AI SIEM. This value should reflect the vendor of the data being inserted. Don't quote this value. The default is cribl.

data_source_vendor_expression.description: Define the dataSource.vendor for events using a JavaScript expression. This value should reflect the vendor of the data being inserted into AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'Cisco' or 'Microsoft').

endpoint.description: Endpoint to send events to. Use /services/collector/event for structured JSON payloads with standard HEC top-level fields. Use /services/collector/raw for unstructured log lines (plain text).

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

event_type.description: Specify the event.type value to pass as an optional parameter to AI SIEM. This value acts as a label, grouping events into meaningful categories like Process Creation, File Modification, or Network Connection. Don't quote this value. By default, this field is empty.

event_type_expression.description: Optionally, define the event.type for events using a JavaScript expression. This value acts as a label, grouping events into meaningful categories. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'Process Creation' or 'Network Connection').

extra_http_headers.description: Headers to add to all events

flush_period_sec.description: Maximum time between requests. Small values could cause the payload size to be smaller than the configured Body size limit.

host.description: Define the serverHost for events using a JavaScript expression. This value will be passed to AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'myServerName').

host_expression.description: Define serverHost for events using a JavaScript expression. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'myServer').

max_payload_events.description: Maximum number of events to include in the request body. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_payload_size_kb.description: Maximum size, in KB, of the request body

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

pq_max_backpressure_sec.description: How long (in seconds) to wait for backpressure to resolve before engaging the queue

pq_max_buffer_size.description: Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use pqMaxBufferSizeBytes instead.

pq_max_buffer_size_bytes.description: The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 1MB.

pq_max_file_size.description: The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing (KB, MB, etc.)

pq_max_size.description: The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.

pq_path.description: The location for the persistent queue files. To this field's value, the system will append: /<worker-id>/<output-id>.

pq_rate_per_sec.description: Throttling rate (in events per second) to impose while writing to Destinations from PQ. Defaults to 0, which disables throttling.

pq_strict_ordering.description: Use FIFO (first in, first out) processing. Disable to forward new events to receivers before queue is flushed.

region.description: The SentinelOne region to send events to. In most cases you can find the region by either looking at your SentinelOne URL or knowing what geographic region your SentinelOne instance is contained in.

reject_unauthorized.description:
Reject certificates not authorized by a CA in the CA certificate path or by another trusted CA (such as the system's). 
        Enabled by default. When this setting is also present in TLS Settings (Client Side), 
        that value will take precedence.

response_honor_retry_after_header.description: Honor any Retry-After header that specifies a delay (in seconds) no longer than 180 seconds after the retry request. @{product} limits the delay to 180 seconds, even if the Retry-After header specifies a longer delay. When enabled, takes precedence over user-configured retry options. When disabled, all Retry-After headers are ignored.

backoff_rate.description: Base for exponential backoff. A value of 2 (default) means Cribl Stream will retry after 2 seconds, then 4 seconds, then 8 seconds, etc.

http_status.description: The HTTP response status code that will trigger retries

initial_backoff.description: How long, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should wait before initiating backoff. Maximum interval is 600,000 ms (10 minutes).

max_backoff.description: The maximum backoff interval, in milliseconds, Cribl Stream should apply. Default (and minimum) is 10,000 ms (10 seconds); maximum is 180,000 ms (180 seconds).

response_retry_settings.description: Automatically retry after unsuccessful response status codes, such as 429 (Too Many Requests) or 503 (Service Unavailable)

safe_headers.description: List of headers that are safe to log in plain text

source.description: Specify the logFile value to pass as a parameter to SentinelOne AI SIEM. Don't quote this value. The default is cribl.

source_expression.description: Define logFile for events using a JavaScript expression. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'myLogFile.txt').

source_type.description: Specify the sourcetype parameter for SentinelOne AI SIEM, which determines the parser. Don't quote this value. For custom parsers, substitute hecRawParser with your parser's name. The default is hecRawParser.

source_type_expression.description: Define the parser for events using a JavaScript expression. This value helps parse data into AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'dottedJson'). For custom parsers, substitute 'dottedJson' with your parser's name.

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

flush_period_sec.description: Maximum time between requests. Small values could cause the payload size to be smaller than the configured Body size limit.

keep_alive.description: Disable to close the connection immediately after sending the outgoing request

protocol_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request protocol as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

referer_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request referer as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

remote_ip_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request remote IP as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_method_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request method as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_size_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request size as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

request_url_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request URL as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

resource_type_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the managed resource type field. Must evaluate to one of the valid values [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/api/v2/resource-list#resource-types). Defaults to "global".

value_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the label's value.

resource_type_labels.description: Labels to apply to the managed resource. These must correspond to the valid labels for the specified resource type (see [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/api/v2/resource-list#resource-types)). Otherwise, they will be dropped by Google Cloud Logging.

response_size_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP response size as a string, in int64 format. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

secret.description: Select or create a stored text secret

server_ip_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request server IP as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

service_account_credentials.description: Contents of service account credentials (JSON keys) file downloaded from Google Cloud. To upload a file, click the upload button at this field's upper right.

severity_expression.description: JavaScript expression to compute the value of the severity field. Must evaluate to one of the severity values supported by Google Cloud Logging [here](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logseverity) (case insensitive). Defaults to "DEFAULT".

span_id_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the ID of the cloud trace span associated with the current operation in which the log is being written as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

status_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request method as a number. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

streamtags.description: Tags for filtering and grouping in @{product}

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

throttle_rate_req_per_sec.description: Maximum number of requests to limit to per second.

timeout_sec.description: Amount of time, in seconds, to wait for a request to complete before canceling it.

total_memory_limit_kb.description: Maximum total size of the batches waiting to be sent. If left blank, defaults to 5 times the max body size (if set). If 0, no limit is enforced.

total_splits_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry log split total splits as a number. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logsplit) for details.

trace_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the REST resource name of the trace being written as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

trace_sampled_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the the sampling decision of the span associated with the log entry. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry) for details.

uid_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the log entry log split UID as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#logsplit) for details.

user_agent_expression.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to the HTTP request user agent as a string. See the [documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/LogEntry#httprequest) for details.

automatic_schema.description: Automatically calculate the schema based on the events of each Parquet file generated

aws_api_key.description: HMAC access key. This value can be a constant or a JavaScript expression, such as `${C.env.GCS_ACCESS_KEY}`.

aws_secret.description: Select or create a stored secret that references your access key and secret key

aws_secret_key.description: HMAC secret. This value can be a constant or a JavaScript expression, such as `${C.env.GCS_SECRET}`.

base_file_name.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename prefix (can be constant)

bucket.description: Name of the destination bucket. This value can be a constant or a JavaScript expression that can only be evaluated at init time. Example of referencing a Global Variable: `myBucket-${C.vars.myVar}`.

deadletter_enabled.description: If a file fails to move to its final destination after the maximum number of retries, move it to a designated directory to prevent further errors

deadletter_path.description: Storage location for files that fail to reach their final destination after maximum retries are exceeded

dest_path.description: Prefix to prepend to files before uploading. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at init time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myKeyPrefix-${C.vars.myVar}`

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

endpoint.description: Google Cloud Storage service endpoint

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

file_name_suffix.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename suffix (can be constant).  The `__format` variable refers to the value of the `Data format` field (`json` or `raw`).  The `__compression` field refers to the kind of compression being used (`none` or `gzip`).

force_close_on_shutdown.description: Force all staged files to close during an orderly Node shutdown. This triggers immediate upload of in-progress data — regardless of idle time, file age, or size thresholds — to minimize data loss.

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

partition_expr.description: JavaScript expression defining how files are partitioned and organized. Default is date-based. If blank, Stream will fall back to the event's __partition field value – if present – otherwise to each location's root directory.

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

region.description: Region where the bucket is located

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

backoff_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to backoff delay after each retry. Valid range: 1-10. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

jitter_percent.description: Random jitter percentage added to backoff delay to prevent thundering herd. Valid range: 0-100. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance

should_log_invalid_rows.description: Log up to 3 rows that @{product} skips due to data mismatch

stage_path.description: Filesystem location in which to buffer files, before compressing and moving to final destination. Use performant and stable storage.

streamtags.description: Tags for filtering and grouping in @{product}

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

verify_permissions.description: Disable if you can access files within the bucket but not the bucket itself

write_high_water_mark.description: Buffer size used to write to a file

batch_size.description: The maximum number of items the Google API should batch before it sends them to the topic.

batch_timeout.description: The maximum amount of time, in milliseconds, that the Google API should wait to send a batch (if the Batch size is not reached).

create_topic.description: If enabled, create topic if it does not exist.

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

flush_period.description: Maximum time to wait before sending a batch (when batch size limit is not reached)

max_in_progress.description: The maximum number of in-progress API requests before backpressure is applied.

max_queue_size.description: Maximum number of queued batches before blocking.

max_record_size_kb.description: Maximum size (KB) of batches to send.

ordered_delivery.description: If enabled, send events in the order they were added to the queue. For this to work correctly, the process receiving events must have ordering enabled.

pq_max_buffer_size_bytes.description: The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 1MB.

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

duration_seconds.description: Duration of the assumed role's session, in seconds. Minimum is 900 (15 minutes), default is 3600 (1 hour), and maximum is 43200 (12 hours).

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_assume_role.description: Use Assume Role credentials to access S3

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

endpoint.description: Amazon Security Lake service endpoint. If empty, defaults to the AWS Region-specific endpoint. Otherwise, it must point to Amazon Security Lake-compatible endpoint.

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

force_close_on_shutdown.description: Force all staged files to close during an orderly Node shutdown. This triggers immediate upload of in-progress data — regardless of idle time, file age, or size thresholds — to minimize data loss.

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

kms_key_id.description: ID or ARN of the KMS customer-managed key to use for encryption

max_closing_files_to_backpressure.description: Maximum number of files that can be waiting for upload before backpressure is applied

max_concurrent_file_parts.description: Maximum number of parts to upload in parallel per file. Minimum part size is 5MB.

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

region.description: Region where the Amazon Security Lake is located.

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

backoff_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to backoff delay after each retry. Valid range: 1-10. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

jitter_percent.description: Random jitter percentage added to backoff delay to prevent thundering herd. Valid range: 0-100. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance

should_log_invalid_rows.description: Log up to 3 rows that @{product} skips due to data mismatch

stage_path.description: Filesystem location in which to buffer files, before compressing and moving to final destination. Use performant and stable storage.

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards. These fields are added as dimensions and labels to generated metrics and logs, respectively.

verify_permissions.description: Disable if you can access files within the bucket but not the bucket itself

write_high_water_mark.description: Buffer size used to write to a file

custom_event_delimiter.description: Delimiter string to insert between individual events. Defaults to newline character.

endpoint_urlconfiguration.description: Enter the data collection endpoint URL or the individual ID

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

max_closing_files_to_backpressure.description: Maximum number of files that can be waiting for upload before backpressure is applied

max_concurrent_file_parts.description: Maximum number of parts to upload in parallel per file. Minimum part size is 5MB.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

partition_expr.description: JavaScript expression defining how files are partitioned and organized. Default is date-based. If blank, Stream will fall back to the event's __partition field value – if present – otherwise to each location's root directory.

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

backoff_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to backoff delay after each retry. Valid range: 1-10. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance

should_log_invalid_rows.description: Log up to 3 rows that @{product} skips due to data mismatch

request_timeout.description: HTTP request inactivity timeout. Use 0 to disable.

codes.description: List of HTTP codes that trigger a retry. Leave empty to use the default list of 429 and 503.

enable_header.description: Honor any Retry-After header that specifies a delay (in seconds) or a timestamp after which to retry the request. The delay is limited to 20 seconds, even if the Retry-After header specifies a longer delay. When disabled, all Retry-After headers are ignored.

interval.description: Time interval between failed request and first retry (kickoff). Maximum allowed value is 20,000 ms (1/3 minute).

limit.description: The maximum number of times to retry a failed HTTP request

multiplier.description: Base for exponential backoff, e.g., base 2 means that retries will occur after 2, then 4, then 8 seconds, and so on

retry_connect_reset.description: Retry request when a connection reset (ECONNRESET) error occurs

retry_connect_timeout.description: Make a single retry attempt when a connection timeout (ETIMEDOUT) error occurs

send_to_routes.description: Select whether to send data to Routes, or directly to Destinations.

stale_channel_flush_ms.description: How long (in milliseconds) the Event Breaker will wait for new data to be sent to a specific channel before flushing the data stream out, as is, to the Pipelines

state_merge_expression.description: JavaScript expression that defines which state to keep when merging a task's newly reported state with previously saved state. Evaluates `prevState` and `newState` variables, resolving to the state to keep.

state_tracking.description: Track collection progress between consecutive scheduled executions

state_update_expression.description: JavaScript expression that defines how to update the state from an event. Use the event's data and the current state to compute the new state. See [Understanding State Expression Fields](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/collectors-rest#state-tracking-expression-fields) for more information.

file_filter.description: Regex matching file names to download and process. Defaults to: .*

num_receivers.description: How many receiver processes to run. The higher the number, the better the throughput - at the expense of CPU overhead.

queue_name.description: The storage account queue name blob notifications will be read from. service_period_secs.description: The duration (in seconds) which pollers should be validated and restarted if exited

automatic_schema.description: Automatically calculate the schema based on the events of each Parquet file generated

base_file_name.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename prefix (can be constant)

bucket.description: Name of the destination S3 bucket. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at initialization time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myBucket-${C.vars.myVar}`

deadletter_enabled.description: If a file fails to move to its final destination after the maximum number of retries, move it to a designated directory to prevent further errors

deadletter_path.description: Storage location for files that fail to reach their final destination after maximum retries are exceeded

dest_path.description: Prefix to prepend to files before uploading. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at init time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myKeyPrefix-${C.vars.myVar}`

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

duration_seconds.description: Duration of the assumed role's session, in seconds. Minimum is 900 (15 minutes), default is 3600 (1 hour), and maximum is 43200 (12 hours).

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_assume_role.description: Use Assume Role credentials to access S3

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

endpoint.description: S3 service endpoint. If empty, defaults to the AWS Region-specific endpoint. Otherwise, it must point to S3-compatible endpoint.

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

file_name_suffix.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename suffix (can be constant).  The `__format` variable refers to the value of the `Data format` field (`json` or `raw`).  The `__compression` field refers to the kind of compression being used (`none` or `gzip`).

force_close_on_shutdown.description: Force all staged files to close during an orderly Node shutdown. This triggers immediate upload of in-progress data — regardless of idle time, file age, or size thresholds — to minimize data loss.

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

kms_key_id.description: ID or ARN of the KMS customer-managed key to use for encryption

max_closing_files_to_backpressure.description: Maximum number of files that can be waiting for upload before backpressure is applied

max_concurrent_file_parts.description: Maximum number of parts to upload in parallel per file. Minimum part size is 5MB.

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

partitioning_fields.description: List of fields to partition the path by, in addition to time, which is included automatically. The effective partition will be YYYY/MM/DD/HH/<list/of/fields>.

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

region.description: Region where the S3 bucket is located

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

jitter_percent.description: Random jitter percentage added to backoff delay to prevent thundering herd. Valid range: 0-100. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance

should_log_invalid_rows.description: Log up to 3 rows that @{product} skips due to data mismatch

stage_path.description: Filesystem location in which to buffer files, before compressing and moving to final destination. Use performant and stable storage.

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

verify_permissions.description: Disable if you can access files within the bucket but not the bucket itself

reauthentication_threshold.description: Specifies a time window during which @{product} can reauthenticate if needed. Creates the window measuring backward from the moment when credentials are set to expire.

base_file_name.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename prefix (can be constant)

bucket.description: Name of the destination Nutanix Objects bucket. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at initialization time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myBucket-${C.vars.myVar}`

deadletter_enabled.description: If a file fails to move to its final destination after the maximum number of retries, move it to a designated directory to prevent further errors

deadletter_path.description: Storage location for files that fail to reach their final destination after maximum retries are exceeded

dest_path.description: Prefix to prepend to files before uploading. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at init time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myKeyPrefix-${C.vars.myVar}`

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

endpoint.description: Nutanix Objects S3-compatible endpoint URL (example: https://objects.nutanix.local)

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

file_name_suffix.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename suffix (can be constant).  The `__format` variable refers to the value of the `Data format` field (`json` or `raw`).  The `__compression` field refers to the kind of compression being used (`none` or `gzip`).

force_close_on_shutdown.description: Force all staged files to close during an orderly Node shutdown. This triggers immediate upload of in-progress data — regardless of idle time, file age, or size thresholds — to minimize data loss.

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

max_closing_files_to_backpressure.description: Maximum number of files that can be waiting for upload before backpressure is applied

max_concurrent_file_parts.description: Maximum number of parts to upload in parallel per file. Minimum part size is 5MB.

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

partition_expr.description: JavaScript expression defining how files are partitioned and organized. Default is date-based. If blank, Stream will fall back to the event's __partition field value – if present – otherwise to each location's root directory.

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

jitter_percent.description: Random jitter percentage added to backoff delay to prevent thundering herd. Valid range: 0-100. Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

should_log_invalid_rows.description: Log up to 3 rows that @{product} skips due to data mismatch

system_fields.description: Fields to automatically add to events, such as cribl_pipe. Supports wildcards.

verify_permissions.description: Disable if you can access files within the bucket but not the bucket itself

write_high_water_mark.description: Buffer size used to write to a file

data_source_vendor.description: Specify the dataSource.vendorvalue to pass as a parameter to AI SIEM. This value should reflect the vendor of the data being inserted. Don't quote this value. The default is cribl.

data_source_vendor_expression.description: Define the dataSource.vendor for events using a JavaScript expression. This value should reflect the vendor of the data being inserted into AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'Cisco' or 'Microsoft').

endpoint.description: Endpoint to send events to. Use /services/collector/event for structured JSON payloads with standard HEC top-level fields. Use /services/collector/raw for unstructured log lines (plain text).

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

event_type.description: Specify the event.type value to pass as an optional parameter to AI SIEM. This value acts as a label, grouping events into meaningful categories like Process Creation, File Modification, or Network Connection. Don't quote this value. By default, this field is empty.

event_type_expression.description: Optionally, define the event.type for events using a JavaScript expression. This value acts as a label, grouping events into meaningful categories. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'Process Creation' or 'Network Connection').

extra_http_headers.description: Headers to add to all events

flush_period_sec.description: Maximum time between requests. Small values could cause the payload size to be smaller than the configured Body size limit.

host.description: Define the serverHost for events using a JavaScript expression. This value will be passed to AI SIEM. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'myServerName').

host_expression.description: Define serverHost for events using a JavaScript expression. You must enclose text constants in quotes (such as, 'myServer').

max_payload_events.description: Maximum number of events to include in the request body. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_payload_size_kb.description: Maximum size, in KB, of the request body

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

pq_max_backpressure_sec.description: How long (in seconds) to wait for backpressure to resolve before engaging the queue

pq_max_buffer_size.description: Maximum number of events to hold in memory before writing the events to disk. Deprecated and only supported in workers < v4.17.0. Use pqMaxBufferSizeBytes instead.

pq_max_buffer_size_bytes.description: The maximum size to hold in memory before writing events to disk. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc. The minimum value is 64KB and the maximum value is 1MB.

pq_max_file_size.description: The maximum size to store in each queue file before closing and optionally compressing (KB, MB, etc.)

pq_max_size.description: The maximum disk space that the queue can consume (as an average per Worker Process) before queueing stops. Enter a numeral with units of KB, MB, etc.

pq_path.description: The location for the persistent queue files. To this field's value, the system will append: /<worker-id>/<output-id>.

pq_rate_per_sec.description: Throttling rate (in events per second) to impose while writing to Destinations from PQ. Defaults to 0, which disables throttling.

pq_strict_ordering.description: Use FIFO (first in, first out) processing. Disable to forward new events to receivers before queue is flushed.

region.description: The SentinelOne region to send events to. In most cases you can find the region by either looking at your SentinelOne URL or knowing what geographic region your SentinelOne instance is contained in.

aws_secret_key.description: Secret key. This value can be a constant or a JavaScript expression. Example: `${C.env.SOME_SECRET}`)

base_file_name.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename prefix (can be constant)

bucket.description: Name of the destination R2 bucket. This value can be a constant or a JavaScript expression that can only be evaluated at init time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myBucket-${C.vars.myVar}`

deadletter_enabled.description: If a file fails to move to its final destination after the maximum number of retries, move it to a designated directory to prevent further errors

deadletter_path.description: Storage location for files that fail to reach their final destination after maximum retries are exceeded

dest_path.description: Prefix to prepend to files before uploading. Must be a JavaScript expression (which can evaluate to a constant value), enclosed in quotes or backticks. Can be evaluated only at init time. Example referencing a Global Variable: `myKeyPrefix-${C.vars.myVar}`

directory_batch_size.description: Number of directories to process in each batch during cleanup of empty directories. Minimum is 10, maximum is 10000. Higher values may require more memory.

empty_dir_cleanup_sec.description: How frequently, in seconds, to clean up empty directories

enable_page_checksum.description: Parquet tools can use the checksum of a Parquet page to verify data integrity

enable_statistics.description: Statistics profile an entire file in terms of minimum/maximum values within data, numbers of nulls, etc. You can use Parquet tools to view statistics.

enable_write_page_index.description: One page index contains statistics for one data page. Parquet readers use statistics to enable page skipping.

endpoint.description: Cloudflare R2 service URL (example: https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com)

environment.description: Optionally, enable this config only on a specified Git branch. If empty, will be enabled everywhere.

file_name_suffix.description: JavaScript expression to define the output filename suffix (can be constant).  The `__format` variable refers to the value of the `Data format` field (`json` or `raw`).  The `__compression` field refers to the kind of compression being used (`none` or `gzip`).

force_close_on_shutdown.description: Force all staged files to close during an orderly Node shutdown. This triggers immediate upload of in-progress data — regardless of idle time, file age, or size thresholds — to minimize data loss.

header_line.description: If set, this line will be written to the beginning of each output file

key_value_metadata.description: The metadata of files the Destination writes will include the properties you add here as key-value pairs. Useful for tagging. Examples: "key":"OCSF Event Class", "value":"9001"

max_closing_files_to_backpressure.description: Maximum number of files that can be waiting for upload before backpressure is applied

max_concurrent_file_parts.description: Maximum number of parts to upload in parallel per file. Minimum part size is 5MB.

max_file_idle_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to keep inactive files open. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_open_time_sec.description: Maximum amount of time to write to a file. Files open for longer than this will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum uncompressed output file size. Files of this size will be closed and moved to final output location.

max_open_files.description: Maximum number of files to keep open concurrently. When exceeded, @{product} will close the oldest open files and move them to the final output location.

max_retry_num.description: The maximum number of times a file will attempt to move to its final destination before being dead-lettered

disabled.description: Periodically scan the staging directory for files not tracked by any Worker manifest to recover them

parquet_page_size.description: Target memory size for page segments, such as 1MB or 128MB. Generally, lower values improve reading speed, while higher values improve compression.

parquet_row_group_length.description: The number of rows that every group will contain. The final group can contain a smaller number of rows.

parquet_schema.description: To add a new schema, navigate to Processing > Knowledge > Parquet Schemas

partition_expr.description: JavaScript expression defining how files are partitioned and organized. Default is date-based. If blank, Stream will fall back to the event's __partition field value – if present – otherwise to each location's root directory.

pipeline.description: Pipeline to process data before sending out to this output

reject_unauthorized.description: Reject certificates that cannot be verified against a valid CA, such as self-signed certificates

remove_empty_dirs.description: Remove empty staging directories after moving files

enabled.description: Apply exponential backoff with jitter when file uploads fail repeatedly.

initial_backoff_ms.description: Initial delay before first retry attempt. Valid range: 1s-5min (1000-300000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

max_backoff_ms.description: Maximum delay between retry attempts. Valid range: 1s-10min (1000-600000ms). Values outside this range will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

reuse_connections.description: Reuse connections between requests, which can improve performance
